subject: Day 41: attend the postpartum visit
bodyText:
Today's focus
Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit anchors the week. Expect exercise clearance for an uncomplicated delivery, a contraception discussion, and a final EPDS depression screen, while Avi's crying continues tapering off its peak.

Action items
- Attend the 6-week postpartum visit with written questions on pelvic floor symptoms, mood, return to exercise, contraception, and the return-to-work date. Noah should attend, since partner presence and support is the single most protective factor against postpartum depression. ACOG: postpartum birth control: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-birth-control
- Decide contraception at this visit. Progestin-only options, including the mini-pill, IUD, and implant, are compatible with breastfeeding, while combined estrogen products are usually deferred until weaning. ACOG: postpartum birth control: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-birth-control
- If Anoushka scores above 10 on the EPDS, ask for a referral today rather than waiting. Postpartum Support International keeps a directory of specialized therapists and a helpline. Postpartum Support International: https://www.postpartum.net/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hair shedding starting around now and light yellowish-white lochia tapering off are both expected parts of recovery.
- [monitor] Persistent low mood, loss of interest, or intrusive worry lasting beyond two weeks. Raise an EPDS above 10 with the OB; PPD most commonly presents weeks 2 through 8.
- [call within 24h] For Anoushka, soaking more than one pad an hour for over two hours, a fever, or calf pain. For Avi, poor feeding plus lethargy plus decreased output together.
- [call now] For Avi, a rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, or blue lips. For Anoushka, thoughts of harming herself or the baby, or chest pain and shortness of breath. Call 988 or 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Set up or refresh a high-contrast mobile so it stays novel as Avi's visual tracking sharpens. He now prefers faces and bold patterns and follows objects further across his field of view. AAP HealthyChildren: baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Place a baby-safe mirror at Avi's eye level during tummy time. Face-tracking is the strongest motivator for the head lifts that build toward steady head control. AAP HealthyChildren: tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Respond to each of Avi's coos as if he spoke, pause two to three seconds, then answer his next sound. These conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language outcomes. PubMed: Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 56-70 (Jul 6-20): 2-month well visit; vaccines due are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (Jul 7-22): the 24-48h post-vaccine window, when low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness are expected.
- Day 84-91 (early August): the sleep consolidation window opens around 3 months, a good time to firm up a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (Aug 31-Sep 14): 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
